Larry Williams: the printed systems, run forward

Lock and deviations · Both coins · Full ledger · Reopen tests · Code and data
Episode A04 · report format v2 · lab run 2026-06-13, pre-registration locked 2026-06-13 before the run
VERDICT — No validated edge on the data we could afford — REPRO-UNGATED

The primary bond rule made -$190,766.40; the range-stop interpretation made +$110,987.90. Both trail the registered coin that buys at the open. A second coin, added after the run and filled at the rule's prices, has lower medians than either rule. That changes the explanation: the first comparison does not isolate signal quality. The calendar rule made +$74,385.00, between its random-day control median and 95th percentile. None of this reproduces the book's printed cells on pit-session data.

What we granted, and what we actually tested

Granted, not measured: Williams printed executable rules and his own results. The subject is two printed systems, not the trader or his current record. The championship record and the later family result are granted as attributed accounts, not independently certified by us; no primary audit document is on file.

Tested: Two of eight reproduction-grade book families, at one contract, on Yahoo Finance 24-hour daily futures composites after publication. Both primary systems use two trade-handling treatments of the same prices. The range-stop sensitivity and the second coin use Arm-A only. Costs and a Yahoo ^IRX cash benchmark are included.

What this report does NOT claim: No claim about his current trading, discretion, remaining systems or paid instruction. We never ran the Pinnacle day-session reproduction on his own printed windows. We cannot distinguish a lost edge from a mismatched data/implementation instrument on this evidence.

§1 · The locked pre-registration

Committed 028efc0 on 2026-06-13, before the probe was run ; execution was committed as 20ba677 later that evening. The post-hoc control is dated 2026-09-18.

The falsifiable question

Do the two printed rules clear a stated after-cost floor, cash and randomized-entry controls on post-publication data, while the two data treatments agree?

  • A yes looks like: Both treatments agree, the rule clears cash and friction, exceeds its control threshold, has plausible cadence and does not depend on one winning year. This still would not substitute for the printed-cell reproduction gate.
  • A no looks like: A rule below the floor yields a screen-tier finding only. Data-treatment disagreement would make the screen inconclusive.
  • Ambiguous residue: Positive returns can fail a control. A stop-reading sign flip must be shown. Unrun printed-cell reproduction caps every conclusion.

Our stated prior: A faithful screen is worth distinguishing from our earlier bot

The protocol was a falsifiable screen, not a numerical probability forecast. The decision criteria and ambiguity rules were written before execution. The later same-fill control is explicitly outside that commitment.

Untested scope and when it was identified

  1. Other six book families, discretionary filters and money management; the bot previously built in his name.
  2. His own historical windows and pit session: the paid reproduction gate was deferred in the lock.
  3. Independent source data was intended but not obtained; Arm-B is the documented same-vendor substitute.
  4. Direction re-flipped at the fill: identified after the second coin, remains unrun.
The lock specified positive-but-below-cash as weak, conflicting A/C arm signs as inconclusive, and stop-interpretation flips as unresolved sensitivity. Later controls did not rewrite that lock.

The second coin samples touched day/side pairs at the breakout price. Conditional on a single-side touch, the fill already fixes breakout direction. It tests sequencing and price, not an independent direction choice. It permits overlapping positions; the real rule does not. Its primary form includes both-touched days; applying the real tie-break materially lowers the apparent percentile. The 60-bar cap drops no same-fill pair on this dataset. Neither a median comparison nor this post-hoc percentile is a new registered validation gate.

§5 · The strongest objection and what remains unrun

The strongest objection is correct: a pit-session rule was run on a 24-hour Yahoo composite, the stop sentence has two readings, and the printed-cell reproduction was not run. The alternative stop is shown because it changes the sign. The second coin changes the story about the driver. The unrun Pinnacle experiment remains the clearest way to lift the ceiling.

Other implementation limits: daily bars cannot order every intraday touch; stop fills use their level despite gaps. Real trades are sequential while null trades may overlap. Null walks stop after 60 bars. Terminal unresolved positions do not become completed ledger trades. Cash compounds the Yahoo ^IRX discount-rate Close divided by 100 and 252, forward/back-filled to futures dates; it is an approximation, not a total-return T-bill series. Arm-B is not independent-price replication.

The printed figures are his attributed cells, not ours and not a matched decay comparison. The first edition identifies the rule, session, windows and zero-cost assumption. Two systems out of eight were tested. No page scan is redistributed.

§8 · What would change our mind

  1. Pinnacle reproduction: obtain day-session data covering the printed years and apply the locked tolerances before rerunning forward. Publish either outcome. The historical $99 quote was recorded in June 2026; no purchase or current-price verification is claimed.
  2. Stop interpretation: if reproduction establishes that the range stop was the printed implementation, promote that reading and correct our primary account. It beat the second coin median but remained below the registered at-open coin; the controls answer different questions.
  3. Mechanical family rules: if the newer family rules become public and executable, register a separate faithful test. Reported championship performance is not reproduced here.
  4. The other six: test the six remaining reproduction-grade book families one at a time, under the same stated discipline. No verdict on those unrun systems.
  5. A direction control: a new, separately registered experiment would re-flip direction at the same touched prices, including fades. The present second coin does not do this. This criterion arose after the run.

§9 · What survives

The calendar system and the alternative range-stop rule made money on these data. Williams published enough detail to attempt a test. The control comparison is informative only after naming its fill price and sampling rules. The actionable finding is the unresolved reproduction task, not an instruction to trade either the rule or a coin.

§10 · Tools for your own testing

Everything we make is free — the reports, the ledgers, all of it. The only thing that costs us real money is the market data.

Every numerical market series: Yahoo Finance, accessed through yfinance: ZB=F Treasury-bond futures, ES=F S&P futures, and ^IRX 13-week Treasury-bill discount-rate Close for the cash benchmark. Price bars are daily 24-hour composites with an undocumented vendor roll method; both treatments use the same bars. No Massive, ThetaData, EODHD or Pinnacle data produced these results. Pinnacle was the proposed paid day-session reproduction, never run. The printed target cells and account sizes come from Williams' book; our fees are the locked modelling assumptions, not measured fills.

The original programs reproduced 207 of 207 screen fields and 539 of 539 addendum fields. The downloadable programs preserve 22 of 22 numerical function syntax trees, apart from the string labels named next, and reproduce 745 of 745 archived fields. Runtime/date and an internal issue pointer are excluded; engine/data path labels are normalized to the portable layout, and internal line-number citations are rewritten as the function names they point to, so each one resolves in these files. This validates reproduction of our screen, not reproduction of Williams' printout.

Download screen engine Download post-hoc same-fill program

Requires Python, numpy, pandas and pyarrow. Save the screen download as williams_screen.py; save the second program as addendum/null2_same_fill.py beneath it. Put your licensed, frozen Yahoo snapshots in data/ZB_F.parquet, data/ES_F.parquet (Open, High, Low, Close with a date index) and data/IRX.parquet (Close, date index). Run the screen first, then the addendum. The programs write result JSON locally. If caches are absent, the original engine attempts yfinance; fresh data will not reproduce a frozen historical snapshot. No raw market data is redistributed.
